items.headline: <US Stock Weekly Theme> Energy Storage Systems - TSLA, ENPH, RUN
items.snippet: Mizuho upgraded Albemarle on upward revisions to lithium demand from stationary storage; Benchmark raised 2026 global LCE demand by 12% to 2.1 million tons, BESS demand revised from 92,000 to 270,000 tons.

items.headline: Albemarle has surprising new reason to rally
items.snippet: Albemarle's average realized lithium price jumped 61% to $19.53 per kilogram from $12.17 a year earlier. Energy Storage adjusted EBITDA climbed 229% to $723 million. U.S. operators plan another 14 GW of battery-storage in 2H26, 26 GW in 2027, 14 GW in 2028. A significant danger:

items.headline: Rocket Thrusters on a Road Car Arrive as EV Makers Split Into Winners and Laggards
items.snippet: On October 12, the most active lithium carbonate contract on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange fell 11.8% to 104,740 yuan per ton, lowest in nearly ten months, and Albemarle shares fell 4.2% pre-market. A day later, Mizuho upgraded the stock to Outperform with a $130 price target. Q

items.headline: Albemarle upgraded to Outperform from Neutral at Mizuho
items.snippet: Mizuho upgraded Albemarle to Outperform from Neutral with an unchanged $130 price target. Strong BESS demand has tipped the market balance into favorable territory; Albemarle is the lowest-cost lithium producer.

items.headline: Albemarle price target lowered to $135 from $230 at Argus
items.snippet: Argus lowered its price target on Albemarle to $135 from $230 and keeps a Buy rating. Lithium is up about 67% year over year but well below all-time highs; supply and demand trends appear poised to improve into 2027.
